{ "source_key": "DS-3653", "imported_issue_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002", "title": "[DS-3653] EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)", "body": "Imported from JIRA [DS-3653] created by tom.desair

From 25 May 2018, the new European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) law will apply. This law enforces that personal data of EU citizens can only be gathered legally under strict conditions, for a legitimate purpose. Furthermore, persons or organisations which collect and manage your personal information must protect it from misuse and must respect certain rights of the data owners which are guaranteed by EU law. This also applies to non-EU based organisations. An overview of this new law can be found here https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/data-protection-reform/overview-of-the-gdpr/

The definition of "personal data" is very broad: name, e-mail, location, ip, tweets, pictures, identifiers…

We need to assess how this impacts DSpace and implement improvements to make DSpace compliant with the GDPR. Otherwise organisations using DSpace will risk high EU fines.

Based on my initial reading, these aspects of DSpace are impacted:

  • The information we capture for usage events in the DSpace log files and SOLR statistics core (see https://piwik.pro/blog/how-will-gdpr-affect-your-web-analytics-tracking/)
  • The ability to delete an eperson account even if that eperson is the submitter of certain items.
  • How DSpace stores or logs identifiers (ORCIDs, email, authority control records, ip addresses... )
  • How DSpace does its session management by returning a session ID cookie. In the future this can only be done on explicit consent (see Piwik blog post).
  • Support the right to erase private items linked to a specific eperson (We do not need to support erasure of public items because of the exception "archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific research, historical research or statistical purposes").
", "state": "closed", "updated_at": "2021-08-31T15:50:45Z", "comments": [ { "id": 908751404, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751404", "body": "tdonohue said:

I think we'd need some more detailed advice here from someone more familiar with the regulations behind GDPR, as this ticket is not yet actionable.

That said, a few of the bullets above do relate directly to other previously completed tickets:

  • Deleting EPerson accounts, even if they are a submitter: DS-2081
  • Anonymizing log files (IPs specifically): DS-955

So, it'd be nice to turn this ticket into individual, actionable tickets (and/or move older, related tickets forward). As is, the scope of this ticket seems too large, and needing more detailed information.

 

 

", "created_at": "2017-07-17T15:00:09Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:41Z" }, { "id": 908751405, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751405", "body": "tom.desair said:

You are absolutely right Tim Donohue. This is indeed not a "development" ticket but more a ticket to track and trigger the discussion on GDPR and to analyse the impact on DSpace. Based on that analysis, this will result in multiple sub-tickets to tackle any compliance issues.

We (Atmire) also plan to do some external consultations with GDPR experts. When we learn more, we'll post our findings in this ticket.

", "created_at": "2017-07-18T10:41:32Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:41Z" }, { "id": 908751407, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751407", "body": "bram said:

Putting in the more details needed stage.

", "created_at": "2017-07-19T11:01:53Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:41Z" }, { "id": 908751409, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751409", "body": "gregor.gabriel said:

The GoogleAnalytics-feature is effected as well. The ip-adresses are tracked by GoogleAnalytics.

(for further details see e.g. 

http://www.blastam.com/blog/5-actionable-steps-gdpr-compliance-google-analytics (#2 Turn on IP Anonymization))

", "created_at": "2018-05-02T08:12:10Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:42Z" }, { "id": 908751410, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751410", "body": "cjuergen said:

In order to certify our repository, I've done some basic anonymization for our 5.x instance a couple of years ago, which incorporated:

  • DSpace Logs
    just log the first 2 sections of the ip
    do not log the email of a logged in user, just anonymous or logged in
    (Adjust Tomcat etc. logging, but that should be in the DSpace Docs)
  • Solr logs
    Removing/Reducing ip, kdns, epersonid, submitter, actor
  • StatisticImporter
    remove/reduce ip, epersonid

As for metadata/authority control mentioned above, the dc.description.provenance, holds the email.

Google Analytics should be disabled by default, even if the steps above are incorporated.

If an instance does not register for a key and so on, we still have DS-2904, which might be a nuisance.

", "created_at": "2018-05-02T12:40:05Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:42Z" }, { "id": 908751412, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751412", "body": "tdonohue said:

Claudia Jürgen: Do you happen to have more information around the changes you made to certify your repository?  Are there actual code changes that could come back into DSpace and help it to be GDPR compliant in an "out of the box" way? Or are there some simple configurations (e.g. log4j settings) to tweak?  It'd be nice to see a wiki page that talked about "Configuring DSpace for GDPR" (or similar) where others can learn, contribute, etc.  If folks are willing to contribute to such a Wiki page, I can create it – but, I'm not a GDPR expert myself, so I'd need help on content.

Also, Google Analytics is disabled by default in DSpace. If you want it enabled, you have to manually configure a Google Analytics key (in dspace.cfg or local.cfg): https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-6_x/dspace/config/dspace.cfg#L1933 

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-02T19:10:14Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:42Z" }, { "id": 908751413, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751413", "body": "cjuergen said:

Tim Donohue the anonymization was basically code changes in the LogManager the SolrLogger and StatisticsImporter, for 5.4 which can be made configurable. This was done for a repository certificate not GDPR, but there are overlaps. Some things are out of scope like Tomcat configuration but should be mentioned/documented.

In my opinion DSpace should adopt the principle "Data protection by design and by default" beyond the GDPR regulations. There are  lot of things which might infringe international, European or national law. E.G. the workflow statistics stores individual perfomance data (data protection and work law). DSpace is used all over the world and to cover all  the different regulations will be tricky. Thus being as "lean" and open as possible might be one approach.

So a page where we identify, what we store and how we process it (btw. it is a legal requirement to document it in some cases)  and then sections about how to configure it for GDPR or other legal requirements. Might be a point to think about whether we really need all we store.

There has been an expert report of the German Research Foundation to review the data privacy practices of ORCID

https://orcid.org/blog/2018/04/18/orcid-and-data-privacy-germany

The report has been translated

https://orcid.org/sites/default/files/16bt40v1%20ENG_ORCID_Datenschutzgutachten_irights_2017_Translation.pdf

There are a lot of GDPR checklists around, but many focus on commercial issues. So this might be closer to home.

 

As for Google Analytics it still seems to be on in 5.x

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-services/src/main/resources/config/dspace-defaults.cfg#L23

 

 

 

 

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-03T14:58:56Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:42Z" }, { "id": 908751415, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751415", "body": "tdonohue said:

Claudia Jürgen: thanks for the additional information.  Is there any chance you'd be willing to help us create such a starting point (and I can then help promote the work and try to find additional contributors)?  It sounds like this is an area that you have a good amount of useful knowledge, and, as you are also a DSpace Committer, you might have immediate recommendations for things that DSpace can fix (to become more lean and avoid storing too much personal information).

I'll admit, I'm very interested in seeing this move forward, but I'm only part-time (on DSpace) and most of my time is now devoted towards DSpace 7 efforts. Therefore, I'll need help/support from others to bring this forward.  So, If you are able to help here, I'd appreciate it. If not, I'll have to find a different volunteer.

As for that config in "dspace-defaults.cfg" – that is odd. I don't even know why that configuration exists there.  Are we certain that even gets loaded into the DSpace Configuration (or is it maybe just used by Unit Testing)? If it is getting loaded into the production configuration for DSpace, then we should definitely log a bug for that and immediately fix it by commenting it out.  My expectation was/is that DSpace should NEVER enable Google Analytics by default.

", "created_at": "2018-05-03T15:47:57Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:42Z" }, { "id": 908751416, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751416", "body": "cjuergen said:

@Tim Donohue yes I can create a starting point. Should it go under Strategic Planning, as we need to create a data and privacy policy in general, or should we create a new to category like Discussion/Brainstorming?

 

As for google analytics this is actually used. We had trouble last February, when GA was down, without having enabled it. The bean is activated in 5.x jspui (haven't checked other combinations)

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/spring/applicationContext.xml#L38

The event listener uses it:

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/google/GoogleRecorderEventListener.java#L59

Don't know whether "UA-554232-12" is a default test key and/or actually registers anything.

 

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-04T10:49:45Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751418, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751418", "body": "bram said:

I am not a lawyer/GDPR professional, but based on what I have read so far, and primarily:

https://iapp.org/media/pdf/resource_center/DPN-Guidance-A4-Publication.pdf 

I am personally convinced that:

  • DSpace holds some personal data (names, email addresses, ip addresses).
  • Institutions operating a repository have "Legitimate Interests" for processing those data. These legitimate interests can be used as the lawful basis for processing these personal data. "Public Task" may also apply if the institution is Gov funded/related.

For continuing to log IP addresses, without anonymization, in SOLR, the very specific legitimate interest is future filtering & identification of robot traffic. If you are anonymizing IPs, you will no longer be able to filter out bots in the future, on those logs, if you discover that a specific IP was a bot.

DSpace (and institutions running DSpace) very likely do not have a legitimate interest to log eperson IDs on the usage events like search operations logged in SOLR, I'm talking specifically about:

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/statistics/SolrLogger.java#L402

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/statistics/SolrLogger.java#L490

For workflow events, it could still be useful as legitimate basis for evaluating the actions in the repository from a management/reporting angle.

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-04T11:41:34Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751420, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751420", "body": "cjuergen said:

This ticket is about GDPR, but we should consider more than this. In analyzing and documenting what we store and how we use it, we'll have at least the information for those who got other rules/laws to consider. DSpace is used wordlwide in a variety of scenarios.

Then make it lean and configurable and thus people can consult with their data protection officer/law department and adjust to their rules.

I'm no legal expert either but found few exceptions like click fraud with regards to IP logging. We are allowed to log non personal IP's like bots, but not all in order to later filter them.

The workflow stats might come handy in reporting but might also infringe work law, as they make individual work evaluation possible.

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-04T13:22:42Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751423, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751423", "body": "cjuergen said:

I started a special topic Data Protection and Privacy in our wiki in order to discuss all issues not only GDPR related ones

 

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-04T14:27:59Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751425, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751425", "body": "tdonohue said:

Thanks Claudia Jürgen!  I appreciate your help here, and I think the place you created these wiki pages looks great. I'll help promote this work to others as well.

I'd encourage everyone following this ticket (or finding it later) to contribute to either the wiki pages or by creating JIRA tickets (logging bug tickets for things DSpace definitely shouldn't be doing), etc.  Those are the two best areas to collaborate at this time. 

I'll be keeping an eye on any bugs logged, will flag them as high priority & do my best to help get them into the code quickly. I'll also try and help get more contributors to the wiki, so that we can figure this out together and provide better suggestions to everyone with regards to GDPR and any other regional privacy laws/policies.

 

", "created_at": "2018-05-04T15:02:41Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751427, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751427", "body": "gerrit said:

> How DSpace does its session management by returning a session ID cookie. In the future this can only be done on explicit consent (see Piwik blog post).

Hm, I'm convinced that this Piwik blog post can be misunderstood easily - that blog post is talking about tracking cookies, not cookies in general.

In general, with GDPR, (third-party) tracking cookies require an explicit user opt-in unless those tracking cookies (and their software) fulfill strict criteria (Datensparsamkeit, anonymization/pseudonymization, no personal data sending, purpose is clearly communicated, expectable and scoped).

But first-party non-tracking cookies are fine under GDPR and don't require an explicit opt-in as long as they are required in order to fulfill a service, such as keeping a user logged-in, or maintaining their online shopping cart state.

...

It be great if the DSpace distribution provided a dedicated privacy policy page whose content can be modified by the local operator, e.g. by editing messages_x.xml localization files.

 

Also, during the user registration process, an optional telephone field can be filled out. Is the telephone number used anywhere within DSpace, and if yes, for which purposes? As the GDPR requires to explain for which purposes personal data is collected, I'd like to add an explanation for what the telephone number may be used (besides from the operator's side in order to give a quick call in problematic situations).

", "created_at": "2018-05-14T15:58:46Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751430, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751430", "body": "bram said:

Even though I'm personally not convinced it's required or even necessary to start emailing all your EPeople, some institutions are doing it & I cooked up a template that is based on one of them at

https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/DSPACE/Email+Template%3A+Informing+Registered+DSpace+Users

I think your registered users, based on the right to be informed, can ask you & you have to respond. But that's different from pro-actively emailing all your EPeople.

", "created_at": "2018-05-26T05:44:04Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:43Z" }, { "id": 908751431, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751431", "body": "gerrit said:

Is there a pragmatic way to redact personally identifiable data from the SOLR statistics? http://localhost:8080/solr/statistics/select?q=*%3A*&wt=json&indent=true contains IP addresses and DNS names. Is it okay to execute some SOLR statement that would remove all IP addresses and DNS names, or redact the last octets IP address, e.g. turning 172.16.254.1 to 172.16.0.0?

", "created_at": "2018-06-11T12:30:30Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:44Z" }, { "id": 908751434, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751434", "body": "cjuergen said:

If you still got the original dspace logs (with the offending data) you may adjust the StatisticsImporter and recreate the stats from the logs. Then, for future compliance, adjust the SolrLogger and LogManager and whatever your Apache/Tomcate .. etc. logs.

", "created_at": "2018-06-12T12:31:29Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:44Z" }, { "id": 908751435, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751435", "body": "elorenzo2 said:

I´m not sure (not a legal expert)  about pro-actively emailing e-persons. Some customers are planning to do so. Regardless of to mail or not to email,  I have still have some doubts about the way to catch the consent of the users and the systems we need to develop to manage that.. And a question some customer frequently ask, do we need an soft-opt-in,  a single opt-in or a double opt-in? 

", "created_at": "2018-06-20T08:48:09Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:44Z" }, { "id": 908751436, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751436", "body": "pmuench said:

I suspect Claudia Jürgen and Bram Luyten (Atmire) are referring to methods like https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/218fdcbaf050cffd3a8a1034c3cb50ba25b5a30f/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/statistics/SolrLoggerServiceImpl.java#L284  and https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/218fdcbaf050cffd3a8a1034c3cb50ba25b5a30f/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/statistics/SolrLoggerServiceImpl.java#L361 that need to be changed in order to have GDPR-conformant SOLR statistics, which is exactly what I did.

However, those methods only produce the basic solr document for all statistics entries, and those are augmented with additional information for different types of events. One of those event types is the workflow event: whenever an item changes its state in from submitted to pooled to in-review etc., an event is logged in SOLR, and those documents contain the eperson uuid of the submitter, the reviewer, admin or whoever was linked to an item at a given time.

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/218fdcbaf050cffd3a8a1034c3cb50ba25b5a30f/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/statistics/SolrLoggerServiceImpl.java#L506

https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/218fdcbaf050cffd3a8a1034c3cb50ba25b5a30f/dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/statistics/SolrLoggerServiceImpl.java#L514

 

In one of the recent dev meetings ( https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/DSPACE/DevMtg+2018-10-17 ), there was a discussion regarding deleting of eperson records. One of the questions was whether to delete provenance metadata on items as well if it contains a reference to a person demanding to be removed from the system. The consensus seems to be that it is not necessary and/or desirable to delete that information. 

Could it be argued that the SOLR statistics documenting workflow events are also a kind of provenance information and therefore does not need to be cleaned up?

", "created_at": "2018-11-07T14:03:14Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:44Z" }, { "id": 908751440, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751440", "body": "cjuergen said:

We actually disabled all the person related data from solr workflow as it might infringe work law, depending on the country naturally.

There is more than GDPR to consider.

", "created_at": "2018-11-07T14:19:24Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:44Z" }, { "id": 908751441, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751441", "body": "pmuench said:

I actually forgot to add one more part of my immediate problem: If it is prudent to disable workflow statistics at least in Germany/Europe, can I simply do so, or are there other parts of dspace depending on those statistics records? If, on the other hand, there is no need to keep that data out of SOLR, the previous question is moot.

Claudia Jürgen, since you said that you disabled all eperson uuid logging in SOLR, that could be the answer, actually.

On a broader perspective, considering taking work law constraints into account as Claudia Jürgen has proposed, the discussion about the deletion and/or deactivation of provenance metadata certainly has to be reopened.

", "created_at": "2018-11-07T14:50:25Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:45Z" }, { "id": 908751442, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751442", "body": "tdonohue said:

Closing as this discussion ticket is no longer needed. A DSpace GDPR Working Group was established to do this analysis. Based on their report, additional improvements are coming in DSpace v7.

", "created_at": "2021-01-07T20:15:21Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:45Z" }, { "id": 908751444, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751444", "body": "Is related to: DS-2081", "created_at": "2017-07-17T11:57:08Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:45Z" }, { "id": 908751446, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/7002#issuecomment-908751446", "body": "Is related to: DS-4070", "created_at": "2017-07-17T11:57:08Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T22:35:45Z" } ] }

{ "source_key": "DS-955", "imported_issue_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/4328", "title": "[DS-955] Anonymize IP-Logging to comply to privacy laws", "body": "Imported from JIRA [DS-955] created by cjuergen

At the moment DSpace logs the complete IP-Addresses in it's log files. Furthermore they are stored/used for Solr statitistics. In some countries this is forbidden based on privacy laws. It should be made possible to anonymize the IP's logged in the log files and adjust solr stats and solr logging.

In the Dspace Logs there are:

  • IP's
  • email address

In the Solr Logs there are:

  • IP's
  • kdns
  • epersonid
  • submitter
  • actor

 

", "state": "closed", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T14:56:01Z", "comments": [ { "id": 908549566, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/4328#issuecomment-908549566", "body": "bram said:

Would there be a way how this could be tackled and still preserving the feature of filtering out bots afterwards based on IP?
If you're going to anonymize IP's, there should be a really good way of identifying whether it's "real" traffic or not at the time of logging, because without the IP information it will be hard to clean out afterwards.

", "created_at": "2011-07-14T18:32:42Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T17:42:32Z" }, { "id": 908549568, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/4328#issuecomment-908549568", "body": "mdiggory said:

I think an approach similar to digesting passwords should lead to enough annonimity to protect users, since we know the bot ip from the lists or user, we can digest that as well and still do bot analysis on the index.

", "created_at": "2011-07-15T05:19:40Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T17:42:32Z" }, { "id": 908549570, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/4328#issuecomment-908549570", "body": "mdiggory said:

for example

public final static byte[] encryptSHA(String s) throws Exception

{ MessageDigest m = null; m= MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-1"); m.reset(); m.update(s.getBytes()); return m.digest(); }", "created_at": "2011-07-15T10:36:32Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T17:42:32Z" }, { "id": 908549571, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/4328#issuecomment-908549571", "body": "tdonohue said:

This idea was discussed in the Developers Meeting on Feb 22, 2012:

[20:07] [ https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/DS-955 ] - DS-955 Anonymize IP-Logging to comply to privacy laws - DuraSpace JIRA
[20:10] Does hashing a 32-bit keyspace really provide much protection?
[20:10] * mdiggory (~mdiggory@rrcs-74-87-47-114.west.biz.rr.com) has joined #duraspace
[20:10] See the concern, not sure DSpace is the place to address it (e.g. still can have IP addrs in Apache logs, etc)
[20:10] to me, this seems like a reasonable request. A part of me wonders though if there's two stages here: (1) hash it initially, (2) after a month (or so) aggregate the stats and just remove specific IPs (once aggregated, we don't really need to keep IP specifics)
[20:11] We are logging IP in both the dspace logs and that the statistics engine. This is more specific to annonymizing those.
[20:12] its important that a number of actions happen prior to anonymization
[20:12] richardrodgers – good point. I agree about the logs. Not sure we should need to anonymize at the log level. I'd be more interested in not storing IPs forever in the stats engine
[20:12] Most important of which is GeoIP evaluation
[20:13] right, but after GeoIP eval is done, why keep around the IP? Can't it just be anonymized to a general location at that point? (or aggregated after a month or so)
[20:14] We've been discussing a solution for distributed statistics aggregation for Dryad, part of which we've proposeda n approach of producing statistics specifc logs that only contain the event data that needs to be placed into solr. This would also act as a backup datasource for DSpace solr based statistics and provide a source for other stats tools as well.
[20:14] these loggs would be generated by the UsageEvent system
[20:14] and update of solr would be a separate process.
[20:15] this is not dissimilar to the current dspace.log stats processing loogic
[20:15] Note the reference to privacy laws. Recall that, just because something is sensible and useful doesn't mean it isn't unlawful.
[20:15] and yes, at that point what was in the log would be anonymized
[20:17] mdiggory: makes sense – yea, I'd assume we'd want to anonymize after GeoIP (or any other initial necessary IP analysis tasks). Is the work you describe for Dryad actually going to be open sourced?
[20:17] one generally wants to reduce risk of any sort of risk of legal action if one can avoid it
[20:18] sorry I was attempting to rewrite that thought before sending it...
[20:18] yes, most everything in Dryad is OS
[20:19] going back to mhwood's question re: hashing a 32-bit keyspace, I think it's sufficient to clear the hurdle of privacy concerns, probably insufficient if you were talking security concerns, though since the specter of legality has been invoked, probably a lawyer would need to weigh in on that
[20:19] the intent is to bring back projects from Dryad whenever it is possible.
[20:21] hpottinger & mhwood, I guess then the question would be whether we should think of providing an option to hash it in the logs – as it sounds like we have some general agreement that once it gets to Stats Engine, to should be anonymized after GeoIP (or similar)
...
[20:22] I'm thinking that we might want to immediately extract aggregated measures such as GeoIP results and just destroy the address altogether – not log anything. If a site has a specific problem then it could (with advice of counsel) insert additional logging to address the specific problem. I think that might satisfy the law very well and not lose much if anything of value.
...
[20:24] mhwood: thats an interesting idea too however, we do retain the ip to post process bots if they are ever added to the bot lists.
[20:25] so we need to be able to produce a hashing strategy to support detecting and cleaning out bots
[20:25] deriving lat/long from IP and then storing that for stats sounds fine... would impact efforts to measure "impact" based on IP address, not sure if that's our concern, making it configurable would be best, not every institution has these concerns
[20:25] mhwood – agreed, interesting idea. I question that we could get all the IP analysis (GeoIP / bot processing) done quickly enough to make it "seemless" though (i.e. we may need to keep that IP temporarily as mdiggory is saying)
[20:26] I"m not sure you got that... the identification of a bot may come long after the logging event itself
[20:26] and theres cli that are responsible for clearing or flagging bot records based on new IP added to the spiders directory
[20:27] mdiggory: I did get that, I'd just say that "long after" is relative. It could be that it's "good enough" for many sites to do bot identification as of today, and then assume it's OK.
[20:27] so, in that case being able to match on records that are bots needs to retain some variant of the IP
[20:28] You may not say that if your stats get bloated with bot events that you can no longer tell were bots.
[20:29] * tdonohue may need to table this discussion shortly. very interesting discussion, but we likely shouldn't take all meeting on it – still, these are great brainstorms
[20:29] ....like the hash of it?
[20:29] remember this is stats, they may be the worse king of lies, but we do try to minimize the error and achieve some level of accuracy
[20:29] Make it configurable? If your local law is persnickety then you turn it off and lose the ability to bot-flag retroactively; otherwise you can turn it on.
[20:30] mdiggory: stats are always 'relative' and accuracy is never a given. The only way to truly be sure about whether an IP could be a bot would be to keep it 'forever' and keep checking (and even then, you still may not be right).
[20:30] I do think there are use cases for keeping some record of an IP address, if it's legal for you to do so, i.e. some researchers might want to know # of downloads from various known institutional ranges
[20:30] hpottinger: interesting point...
[20:31] Yes, but that goes back to the "specific problem" argument: if you want to extract more, add an extractor.
[20:31] I suspect the appropriate case even then is to abstract it to some "state" like" oncampus" / "offcampus"
[20:31] interface StackableLogMassager....
[20:33] could also think about just making it 'semi-anonymous'....cut off the last part of the IP, so that "127.0.0.1" becomes "127.0.0" at some point...then, you still know something about where that came from, but it's not exact. Just a brainstorm
[20:33] in any case, we probably should close up this discussion here shortly
[20:33] mdiggory: requires that you know what you're looking for ahead of time, but I agree, that's probably the best approach
[20:34] * mhwood notes that many many addresses are effectively anonymized at the other end due to dynamic allocation, NAT, etc.
[20:34] The point being, not that we don't need to address this, but that the quality of the data is already iffy.
[20:35] ok, shall we move on to other topics now? We should post these discussion notes to DS-955

", "created_at": "2012-02-23T04:19:57Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T17:42:32Z" }, { "id": 908549575, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/4328#issuecomment-908549575", "body": "cjuergen said:

As for bots the isBot flag is set during solr logging and the flag should be enough to filter out bots. The only pitfall is, if you have already anonymized log files and one tries to generate the statistics out of the logs with the log importer.

", "created_at": "2018-05-02T13:04:09Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T17:42:33Z" } ] }

{ "source_key": "DS-2904", "imported_issue_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/6260", "title": "[DS-2904] Google Analytics recording can fastly exhaust database connection when there are network issues", "body": "Imported from JIRA [DS-2904] created by bollini\n

If the server is not able to reach the google analytics server retrieving bitstreams to show thumbnails or get the actual fulltext hold the database connection for several minutes and retry exhausting the database pool very fastly.

\n\n

The only available workaround is to disable the google analytics listner in the applicationContext.xml

\n\n

As the current implementation doesn't use the http proxy configured to reach the external network this problem is very easy to affect any installation in a private network

", "state": "closed", "updated_at": "2021-10-22T15:14:00Z", "comments": [ { "id": 908725022, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/6260#issuecomment-908725022", "body": "bram said:\n

Marking as needs volunteer. This is still a problem & the description is clear.

", "created_at": "2017-01-07T16:22:58Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T21:49:24Z" }, { "id": 908725024, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/6260#issuecomment-908725024", "body": "cjuergen said:\n

We actually ran into this problem today and it was a nuisance. I wonder why this is not disabled by default and must be enabled. Anyone wishing to use Google Analytics must register, get a key and provide it in dspace.cfg, so one must be \"active\" to enable it anyway.

", "created_at": "2017-02-16T13:33:18Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T21:49:24Z" }, { "id": 908725027, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/6260#issuecomment-908725027", "body": "cjuergen said:\n

Allthought the Google Recorder checks whether a key exists and only then tries to record the event
\nhttps://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-services/src/main/resources/config/dspace-defaults.cfg#L23

\n\n

As a default is configured, this will always happen
\nhttps://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/dspace-5_x/dspace-services/src/main/resources/config/dspace-defaults.cfg#L23

", "created_at": "2017-02-16T16:02:48Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T21:49:24Z" }, { "id": 908725031, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/6260#issuecomment-908725031", "body": "kingkrimmson said:\n

Created a PR to address this issue: https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/pull/2248/files

\n\n

This PR addresses these concerns by queueing up events and processing them in a single asynchronous thread. Events are stored in memory in a CircularFifoBuffer whose size can be limited (by configuration) if desired. A single thread runs in the background, sleeping, and then checking this list. The thread batches these events into sets of up to 20 (the max supported by the GA Collection API) and sends a batch request. When the list is empty, the thread sleeps again.

\n\n

The threading was also designed to finish processing these events when DSpace is shutdown. This solution has been tested and proven to work on a production system with heavy traffic.

", "created_at": "2018-10-26T20:14:05Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T21:49:24Z" }, { "id": 908725036, "html_url": "https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/issues/6260#issuecomment-908725036", "body": "Is related to: DS-2718", "created_at": "2015-11-19T16:19:19Z", "updated_at": "2021-08-30T21:49:25Z" } ] }
